phase1_inventory.source_ref: Figure 1, right panel and caption (paper p. 2; Sec. I)
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Schematic x-y projection of O marking T-type and H-type magic directions; it is a conceptual geometry diagram rather than a numerical result.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Theorem 2 / T-theorem in Sec. I; Eqs. for F_T, epsilon_0 and threshold polarization in Sec. V
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The five-qubit protocol predicts epsilon_0=(1-sqrt(3/7))/2≈0.173, F_T=sqrt((1+sqrt(3/7))/2)≈0.910 and threshold polarization sqrt(3/7)≈0.655, with recursive purification below the unstable fixed point and flow to 1/2 above it.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Theorem 3 / H-theorem in Sec. I; Eq. (37) and Figure 3 discussion in Sec. VI
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: The 15-qubit protocol predicts a nontrivial fixed point epsilon_0≈0.141, equivalently F_H≈0.927 and threshold polarization 2F_H^2-1≈0.718.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. I, definitions and discussion of F_T^* and F_H^*
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Optimization over the stabilizer octahedron gives F_T^*=sqrt((1+sqrt(1/3))/2)≈0.888 and F_H^*=sqrt((1+sqrt(1/2))/2)≈0.924 as lower bounds on possible distillation thresholds.
For two ideal T states the even-parity outcome has probability 2/3, consumes three T states on average under retry, and yields gamma=pi/12 and the phase resource |A_{-pi/6}>.
The hitting-time tail is claimed to scale as c N^{-1/2} on the integer walk and to decrease exponentially for rational theta/(2pi), where the walk is on a finite cyclic group.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. IV, Eqs. (5) and resource-estimate discussion
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: For L non-Clifford gates the paper claims K=O(log L), epsilon_out=O(1/(L log L)), H-distillation raw-state cost n=O((log(1/epsilon_out))^gamma) with gamma=log_3(15)≈2.5, and total raw ancillas N=O(L(log L)^(gamma+1)).

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Figure 2, upper panel (paper p. 9); Eq. (23) in Sec. V
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Numerical curve of the five-qubit T-type one-round output error epsilon_out(epsilon) over 0≤epsilon≤1/2, including the diagonal reference and the nontrivial crossing near epsilon=0.173.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Figure 2, lower panel (paper p. 9); success-probability equation in Sec. V
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Numerical curve of the five-qubit trivial-syndrome success probability p_s(epsilon), claimed monotone from 1/6 at epsilon=0 to 1/16 at epsilon=1/2.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. V, Eqs. (6) and (24) and the yield paragraph following Figure 2
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Small-error behavior epsilon_out≈5 epsilon^2, asymptotic one-level yield r≈1/30, and recursive scaling epsilon_out(n,epsilon)~(5epsilon)^(n^xi) with xi=1/log_2(30)≈0.2.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Figure 3 (paper p. 13); Eqs. (36)-(37) in Sec. VI
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Numerical curve of the 15-qubit H-type one-round output error epsilon_out(epsilon) over 0≤epsilon≤1/2, including the diagonal reference and nontrivial crossing epsilon_0≈0.141.
The 15-qubit protocol success probability is p_s=[1+15(1-2epsilon)^8]/16; it approaches one for small epsilon and implies a small-error yield near 1/15.
Small-error behavior epsilon_out≈35 epsilon^3 and recursive scaling epsilon_out(n,epsilon)~(sqrt(35)epsilon)^(n^xi) with xi=1/log_3(15)≈0.4.

phase1_inventory.source_ref: Sec. VII, concluding paragraph on GF(4)-linear codes
phase1_inventory.scientific_basis: Unpublished numerical simulations for some n=11 and n=17 GF(4)-linear stabilizer codes are claimed to show threshold fidelity increasing with code size relative to the five-qubit scheme.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The paper's five-qubit output-error map, threshold and small-error behavior survive an independent projector construction, exact algebraic factorization, a 70-digit precision check, and a deterministic rerun whose frozen data hash matches the attestation.

independent_checks.claim: A from-scratch 32x32 stabilizer projector built only from the four printed Pauli generators has rank two and yields accepted Hamming-sector weights [1/6,0,5/6,5/6,0,1/6] and decoded-error weights [0,0,5/6,0,0,1/6], independently recovering Eq. (23).

Factoring epsilon_out-e gives -epsilon(epsilon-1)(2epsilon-1)(7epsilon^2-7epsilon+1) over a positive denominator, so the interior root is 0.1726731646460114281; the series begins 5 epsilon^2 and the 2001-row CSV differs from a separate 70-digit evaluation by at most 1.66e-16.
A clean temporary rerun reproduced t_type_curves.csv with SHA-256 7107562a9454c3708668f3330ddf77b969dfe97f5982c47c5923e5e535920553 and the renderer preserved that hash.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The reproduced T-type output map has the paper's logical-sector assignment and fixed point.
falsification_attempts.method: Reconstruct the projector and logical sectors from the printed stabilizers, then factor the fixed-point residual without importing the reproduction module.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The scientific T-type curve is generated without source pixels or author arrays as numerical inputs.
falsification_attempts.method: Inspect the declared provenance, isolated-run input manifest and all recorded file accesses, then rerun the numerical and rendering paths separately.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The lower panel's success probability follows from the same independent projector sector weights; its exact endpoints, monotonicity and complete frozen curve all agree with the paper at paper-exact epsilon range.

independent_checks.claim: Summing independently projected accepted sectors gives p_s=[epsilon^5+5epsilon^2(1-epsilon)^3+5epsilon^3(1-epsilon)^2+(1-epsilon)^5]/6.

The derivative simplifies to 5(2epsilon-1)^3/6, hence p_s is non-increasing on [0,1/2]; direct limits give p_s(0)=1/6 and p_s(1/2)=1/16, and the frozen CSV differs from a 70-digit evaluation by at most 6.24e-17.
The clean rerun reproduced the shared T-type frozen CSV byte-for-byte and the attested actual parameters equal the expected [0,1/2] interval and 2001-point rendering grid.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The lower-panel probability is normalized and satisfies the paper's monotonic endpoint claim.
falsification_attempts.method: Derive p_s from accepted error sectors, differentiate the polynomial, and evaluate both endpoints independently.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: The H-type curve survives an independent punctured Reed-Muller enumeration, symbolic small-error and monotonicity checks, a high-precision fixed-point solve, and a deterministic frozen-data rerun.

independent_checks.claim: A from-scratch truth-table span gives |L1|=16, |L2|=1024 and L1-perp size 2048, with L2 weights [1 at 0, 105 at 4, 280 at 6, 435 at 8, 168 at 10, 35 at 12]; these independently recover Eqs. (35)-(36).

The H-map series is 35epsilon^3+105epsilon^4+378epsilon^5+..., its derivative numerator factors into nonnegative squares on [0,1/2], and a 70-digit bisection gives epsilon_0=0.1414802926561672383, consistent with the paper's 0.141.

At epsilon=10^-2,10^-3,10^-4,10^-5 the independently evaluated epsilon_out/epsilon^3 approaches 36.0877,35.1054,35.0105,35.0011; all 2001 frozen rows agree with 70-digit arithmetic within 1.78e-16 for epsilon_out and 4.87e-16 for p_s.
A clean temporary rerun reproduced h_type_curves.csv with SHA-256 2ebb08e4e0cb1b8896336ca5a9cdff6ff5de273726bffb1f78de62c49df357fe and preserved it through rendering.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The H-type formula uses the paper's Reed-Muller coset orientation and yields its threshold.
falsification_attempts.method: Enumerate L1, L2 and the complemented coset directly from the 15 nonzero four-bit inputs, then recompute success and conditional error without importing the implementation.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The H-type curve remains valid at extended precision without a hidden low-epsilon cancellation or clipping defect.
falsification_attempts.method: Evaluate the printed polynomial at 70-digit precision over the full frozen grid and on a shrinking epsilon sequence.

target_reviews.assessment_reason: Section VII identifies only the lengths n=11 and n=17 and says that 'some' GF(4)-linear codes were simulated. It supplies no generator matrices, logical operators, search ensemble, individual thresholds, tolerances or frozen result arrays. The generic implementation is code-ready but its target config intentionally contains no codes, so the published trend cannot be independently reproduced or falsified.

independent_checks.claim: The reported lengths satisfy the paper's necessary family condition n=6k-1 (k=2 and 3), but that invariant does not uniquely specify a stabilizer code or its threshold map.
The generic signed Pauli-enumerator engine validates its method against the printed five-qubit code, but the empty n=11/n=17 code list prevents a target-specific calculation.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The Section VII trend is uniquely determined by the lengths n=11 and n=17 and can therefore be reconstructed from the paper alone.
falsification_attempts.method: Audit the full source and enumerate the minimum stabilizer/logical data required by the supplied generic threshold engine.

falsification_attempts.hypothesis: The falsification bundle contains frozen n=11/n=17 target data or an attested T004 run despite the empty campaign configuration.
falsification_attempts.method: Compare the bundle manifest, target contract, attestation target lists and generated-data inventory against T004.

findings.claim: The authored numerical scope lists only the three plotted panels and the Section VII code-search claim, but the frozen paper-only inventory identifies nine additional reproducible numeric claims (inv-03 through inv-08, inv-11, inv-13 and inv-14). Several are indirectly calculated in shared evidence, yet none is represented as its own target or explicit deferred item, so the authored scope is not exhaustive under the protocol's quantitative-claim rule.
reproduction_steps: Read Secs. I, III-VI of paper/paper-source/final.tex and enumerate each quantitative claim independently of the authored target list.
Observe that the contract has numeric entries only for Fig. 2 upper, Fig. 2 lower, Fig. 3 and the n=11/n=17 claim; the nine listed inventory IDs have no scope row.

findings.claim: The T-state gate-injection statistics (inv-06) and injection random-walk tail (inv-07) are absent not only from the authored scope but also from the equation cards, frozen quantitative-claims output and scientific checks. Their paper claims therefore have no case-local formula gate or executable falsification evidence.
reproduction_steps: Locate the 2/3 success probability, three-copy average and random-walk tail statements in Sec. III of paper/paper-source/final.tex.
Search formula/EQUATION_CARDS.json for the gate-injection probability, copy cost, integer-walk tail and cyclic-walk tail.
Search generated_data/outputs/data/quantitative_claims.json and machine_evidence/outputs/checks/science_checks.json for corresponding outputs or assertions; none are present.

findings.claim: T004 cannot be scientifically adjudicated from the publication because the exact n=11 and n=17 GF(4)-linear codes or their search definition and numerical results are not supplied; the bundle correctly contains no fabricated substitute, but completion remains blocked.
reproduction_steps: Read the final GF(4)-code paragraph of paper/paper-source/final.tex and record every specified input.
Inspect implementation/config/gf4_threshold_campaign.json and confirm that codes is empty and input_status is blocked_missing_paper_code_generators.
Inspect bundle_manifest.json and both run attestations; confirm that no T004 data file or isolated T004 run exists.

findings.claim: The primary scientific-crop all-pixel scores are above 99 for T001-T003, but the foreground-only similarity is 75.58 for T001 and 75.48 for T003. The independent numerical checks support the science, yet the high-fidelity pixel label is dominated by matching white background and should not be interpreted as line-level agreement.
reproduction_steps: For PXT_T001_SCIENCE and PXT_T003_SCIENCE compare render_acceptance.score with pixel_difference_metrics.foreground_pixel_similarity_score_0_100.
Confirm that implementation/config/render_contract.json locks scientific arrays and that the numerical assessments do not depend on the pixel score.

findings.claim: The restricted bundle's full pytest invocation reports 8 passed and 2 failed because test_render_figures.py expects implementation/outputs, while frozen data are packaged under generated_data and the generated-data manifest is omitted. Direct clean numerical and renderer reruns succeed and reproduce all four scientific hashes, so this is a review-bundle runnability issue rather than a scientific failure.
reproduction_steps: From the extracted bundle run PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider implementation/tests.
Observe both failures are FileNotFoundError for implementation/outputs/data/t_type_curves.csv or h_type_curves.csv in implementation/tests/test_render_figures.py.
Run implementation/scripts/run_reproduction.py to a temporary output root, then implementation/scripts/render_figures.py against that root; compare hashes with bundle_manifest.json.
